featured_reviews.review_text:
Be very careful before buying a flat in Cheeda Greens, Mira Bhayandar.

The sales team promises many facilities during the sales process but does not clearly explain the actual situation. Amenities like gym, garden and other facilities will only be available after all buildings (3, 4 and 5) are completed, which may take 6–7 years.

Parking is a major issue. There is no proper guest parking and very limited two-wheeler parking, which leads to frequent arguments among residents. Many open spaces have been converted into parking. Delivery persons are also not allowed inside the building, so residents must go outside to collect orders.

There are also many hidden clauses in the agreement that are not clearly explained to buyers. Once the flat is purchased, the sales team becomes unresponsive and the builder does not listen to residents’ concerns.

Possession of Building 3 was already delayed by around 2 years, so buyers should be cautious about timelines for other buildings under construction.

Overall, please read the agreement carefully and think twice before investing here.

featured_reviews.review_text:
_MEHNGA CHAWL_
​I am writing this review to warn potential buyers about the reality of living at Chheda Greens. Despite the premium price tag, the living conditions and management are severely lacking. Here are the primary issues:
​1. Construction & Water Quality
​The construction quality is incredibly poor. We have already experienced tiles falling off the walls in the bathrooms. Furthermore, the water supply is unreliable and of low quality, with a TDS level of 500, which is far from ideal for daily consumption and usage.
​2. Parking & Mismanagement
​Parking is a nightmare. There is zero dedicated parking space for many residents, and there isn't even enough room to park one bike per flat. Most shockingly, the management has sold parking spaces directly in front of the wing exits—a clear safety violation and unauthorized practice that obstructs movement.
​3. Non-Functional Infrastructure
​Despite the building being over 70% occupied, the lifts are frequently out of order. This is unacceptable for a modern residential complex and causes massive inconvenience to families and the elderly.
​4. Builder Apathy
​The most frustrating part is the builder's attitude. Despite numerous formal complaints from the residents, the builder refuses to acknowledge the concerns or provide a timeline for fixes.

This project is nothing more than a "mehnga chawl". Do not be fooled by the marketing; the lack of basic amenities and poor construction make it a very poor investment.

featured_reviews.name: Owner
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear Buyer.
The construction and overall appearance of Chheda Green, Avighna Building  is good. However, anyone planning to buy a flat here should think carefully.

Parking is a major issue. If you don’t have a vehicle, then it may be manageable. But if you have a car or even a bike, it becomes very difficult. There is no proper parking provision, and not even one bike parking space per flat. Because of this, residents often have daily arguments over parking.

The builder clearly says there is no bike parking space here — if you want to buy the flat, buy it, otherwise don’t.

Another disappointing part is the developer’s behavior. Once the flat is sold, it feels like their responsibility ends there. The attitude is quite rude and there is very little support or concern shown towards residents after the sale.

And if you also want your day to start with arguments and conflicts over parking, then this might be the perfect place for you to buy a home.

featured_reviews.name: Raju Suthar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Over-promise, delayed possession & unfair payment recovery

Booked a flat in another project of Salasar (Salasar Esquire) in December 2024 based on commitments given by the Nirmal Estate sales team (Manali, Kajal and Ridhhi).

At the time of booking, we were clearly informed that although the RERA possession date was 2026, the project was already 85% complete and possession would be given by June 2025. Based on these assurances, buyers were charged rates similar to near-completed properties.

However, after booking, the possession timeline kept changing continuously:

• June 2025
• August 2025
• October 2025
• December 2025
• March 2026
• Now shifted to Aug 2026

This shows clear over-promising during sales and complete lack of transparency afterward.

Another serious concern is payment recovery.
If the project genuinely required time till July 2026 for completion, then how was the builder able to recover almost 94–95% of the flat value from buyers by August 2025 itself?

This raises a serious concern regarding construction-linked payment justification, as collections were done much faster than the actual construction progress.

Additionally, maintenance charges communicated during booking were around ₹3–4 per sq. ft., payable at possession. Buyers are now being informed that maintenance will be around ₹7 per sq. ft., which was never disclosed earlier.

Now another issue has come up regarding parking. During sales discussions, buyers were informed that there would be open parking available for 2-wheelers. After booking and substantial payment collection, the sales team is now stating that parking will instead be chargeable because the builder has changed the policy.

In my personal opinion, buyers should be extremely careful while dealing with this project and this sales/marketing team. The experience has been highly misleading, with multiple commitments changing after payment collection.

Also, prospective buyers should not blindly rely on online reviews alone. It is better to independently verify facts, speak to actual buyers and insist on written commitments for every important point before making any payment.

Very disappointing experience overall. Buyers should ensure that every promise regarding possession timelines, charges, parking and amenities is documented in writing before booking.
